report_assessment: Minor revision: false ancillary quantitative phase under C1, conditional extension-scope ambiguity, and local proof corrections; main symmetry conclusions not refuted

issues.title: The universal logarithmic phase exceeds the stated C1 assumptions
issues.decisive_evidence: For f(s)=s[1-(1-log(s))^-2], f belongs to C1[0,1], f'(0)=1, f(1)=0 and (f/s)'=-2/[s(1-log(s))^3]<0. Bouin-Henderson arXiv:2009.00698v1 Theorem 1.2(ii), equations (1.4),(1.9), applies with r=3,A=1 to Heaviside data. With alpha=(1+sqrt(5))/2, X(t)=2t-(alpha+1/2)log(t), their iterated upper limit is zero. The printed phase 2t-(3/2)log(t)+constant+o(1) is ahead by (alpha-1)log(t) tending to infinity. Spatial monotonicity gives v(t,zeta_print(t))->0, whereas (4.34) at that point requires phi(0)>0.
issues.impact: Confirmed false quantitative assertion at the standing regularity. Requires explicit correction; severity does not require a counterexample to the whole paper.
issues.repair_boundary: Delete the unsupported precise logarithmic parenthesis or verify additional hypotheses for that separate claim. The constructions use some convergent phase and its leading speed, not this exact coefficient.
issues.counterevidence_limit: No counterexample to Theorems 2.1-2.4 or Propositions 4.4/4.6. The one-dimensional Heaviside example is not a direct counterexample to the p17 bounded-support higher-dimensional formula. External theorem statement and assumptions checked, not its full proof.
issues.impact_boundary: The exact logarithmic coefficient is ancillary. Proposition4.4 only uses convergence with some phase, and Proposition4.6 only its linear speed. No demonstrated core theorem dependency on the false coefficient; severity is based on actual role, not repair length.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Parenthesis after Eq4.34 p21 asserts universal exact3/c* logarithmic delay under standing C1 KPP hypotheses.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Primary independently differentiated f=s[1-(1-log s)^-2] and verified f'(0)=1, positive f, f(1)=0 and (f/s)'<0. The actual retained Bouin-Henderson v1 pp1-3 Theorem1.2(ii) applies with r=3,A=1 and Heaviside initial data. Its iterated ahead-of-front limit plus spatial monotonicity gives v(t,zeta_print(t))->0 since the phase is ahead by(alpha-1)logt, contrary to Eq4.34's positive phi(0).
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: Primary traced actual source pp21-23: Prop4.4 only uses convergence with some phase; Prop4.6 only linear speed and strict angular speed gap. No demonstrated dependence of the core symmetry theorem on the false exact coefficient. Therefore Minor by mathematical role, not by ease of repair. The separate p17 higher-dimensional claim is not declared refuted.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Delete the ancillary exact coefficient or state and justify additional near-zero regularity assumptions. External theorem proof not wholly re-established.

issues.title: Corollary 2.5 general-data extension must explicitly retain thickness

locations.anchor: (8.1) and sentence extending Corollary 2.5; static article2.tex line 1091

issues.decisive_evidence: The two listed finite Hausdorff distances alone allow logistic N2 data 1_S for S=union_{k in Z2,k2<=0} closed B_{exp(-|k|^2)}(k). S is closed with interior seeds, {u0>=h}=supp(u0)=S, and d_H({x2<=0},S)<infinity. Every fixed-thickness core S_delta is bounded or empty. The Proposition 4.6 Gaussian argument gives u(t,x)<=A exp(-|x|+2t). If all Omega profiles were vertical, compactness would give uniform horizontal derivative decay; fixed-radius seed recovery combined with steps 1/(4 eps) every fixed tau produces speed 1/(4 eps tau)>2, a contradiction.
issues.impact: Explicit counterexample to a standalone two-condition reading of the affirmative extension.
issues.repair_boundary: State that the full (8.1), especially d_H({u0>=h},{u0>=h}_delta)<infinity, remains assumed.
issues.counterevidence_limit: If complete (8.1) is already intended to be inherited from the previous paragraph, this is a scope clarification and no refutation of that intended extension. No null-set modification is used.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: The general-data Corollary2.5 extension sentence p31 prints two Hausdorff-distance conditions; preceding Eq8.1 contains a further uniform thickness premise.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For logistic N2 data supported on shrinking closed balls centered on the lower lattice half-space, both displayed distances are finite, but every fixed thickness core is bounded or empty. Weighted initial mass is finite, yielding u(t,x)<=A exp(-|x|+2t). If all limits were vertical, uniform horizontal derivative decay and fixed seed-recovery time would yield arbitrarily large horizontal propagation speeds, contradicting that bound.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The full inherited Eq8.1 interpretation excludes this datum. This is a conditional two-condition counterexample and a scope clarification, not an unconditional refutation of the intended extension. The datum has positive-measure interior, not a null-set support trick.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Explicitly retain the complete high-level-set thickness hypothesis.

issues.title: General-data proof omits one Hausdorff-distance term from L

locations.anchor: L choice for transformed supports following (8.2)

issues.decisive_evidence: Let A={u0>=h}, S=supp u0. The printed L=d_H(A,A_delta)+1 need not reach A_delta from a projection onto S. Two unit balls centered at 0 and 100e1, with values 1 and eps<h, delta=1/4, give printed L=5/4. The projection 100e1+e2 of 100e1+2e2 onto S is at distance sqrt(10001)-3/4 from A_delta.
issues.impact: The printed uniform seed-location constant is insufficient, even though full (8.1) holds.
issues.repair_boundary: Take L>d_H(S,A)+d_H(A,A_delta), e.g. their sum plus 1.
issues.counterevidence_limit: Both distances are finite under the stated complete hypothesis, so the extension proof can be locally repaired.

issues.title: Conjecture 8.1 incorrectly forces both constant profiles in degenerate cases
issues.decisive_evidence: Theorem 2.2 allows U=R^N, giving u=1, E empty and Omega={1}, while the conjectured set contains 0 and 1. U empty gives the opposite single constant; relatively dense thick nonempty supports invade uniformly and likewise omit zero.
issues.impact: Printed conjecture fails at allowed boundary cases.
issues.repair_boundary: Restrict to nonempty, non-relatively-dense supports or retain only constants that actually occur.
issues.counterevidence_limit: This concerns a conjecture, not a proved main theorem.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Conjecture8.1 p31 inherits support scope allowing U=R^N or empty.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: U=R^N gives u identically1 and Omega={1}, whereas the conjectured union also contains0; empty U yields the converse singleton. These meet the allowed boundary cases.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The statement is a conjecture, not a proved main theorem. Nonempty relatively dense thick supports likewise have uniform invasion and omit0.
